advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an `aws:SourceAccount = local.bedrock_cap_account_id` condition to the `AllowCostAlerts` SNS topic-policy statement (in a follow-up change that verifies an anomaly alert still lands), matching the confused-deputy guard already on `AllowBudgetsPublish`.
evidence: Contrast with the sibling grant at infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:212-214: `Condition = { StringEquals = { "aws:SourceAccount" = local.bedrock_cap_account_id } }`

The in-file comment (lines 224-228) and rebar ticket 3d85-eaad-b5e0-4f84 both explicitly note the omission is a deliberate deferral: 'Adding the condition would be a confused-deputy hardening ... it belongs in its own change that can verify an anomaly alert still lands.'
advisory.finding: The new `AllowCostAlerts` SNS:Publish grant for service principal `costalerts.amazonaws.com` omits the `aws:SourceAccount` condition that the sibling `AllowBudgetsPublish` statement carries, leaving the service-principal grant open to cross-account confused-deputy abuse (any account's Cost Anomaly Detection could be induced to publish to this topic).
scenarios: A malicious or misconfigured party in another AWS account triggers Cost Anomaly Detection publishes to this topic, injecting spoofed spend-anomaly alerts to the confirmed email subscriber.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the `AllowCostAlerts` SNS statement with an `aws:SourceAccount` (or `aws:SourceArn`) condition to prevent cross-account confused-deputy publishes, coordinating with delivery verification per the commit's stated follow-up plan.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:229-235: `Sid = "AllowCostAlerts" ... Principal = { Service = "costalerts.amazonaws.com" } Action = "SNS:Publish"` with no `Condition` block
infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:212-214: sibling Budgets grant DOES scope with `StringEquals = { "aws:SourceAccount" = local.bedrock_cap_account_id }`

AWS shared service principals (`*.amazonaws.com`) are identical across all AWS accounts; without a Source* condition the topic policy places no owning-account constraint on which account's Cost Anomaly Detection may invoke SNS:Publish — the documented cross-service confused-deputy shape

Reachability: an actor with Cost Anomaly Detection config in another account can target this topic ARN, injecting spoofed/noise anomaly alerts into the spend-cap alerting channel or drowning genuine alerts

Mitigating context recorded (not exculpatory): commit lines 224-228 state the omission is deliberate to match the live policy exactly and avoid silently altering delivery, deferring the `aws:SourceAccount` hardening to a follow-up change that can verify an alert still lands
advisory.finding: The new `AllowCostAlerts` SNS topic-policy statement grants the shared AWS service principal `costalerts.amazonaws.com` `SNS:Publish` with no `aws:SourceAccount` (or `aws:SourceArn`) condition, leaving a cross-service confused-deputy gap: Cost Anomaly Detection in ANY AWS account can be configured to publish to this account's spend-cap alert topic, whereas the sibling `AllowBudgetsPublish` statement is scoped with `aws:SourceAccount = local.bedrock_cap_account_id`.
scenarios: A Cost Anomaly subscription in an unrelated AWS account is pointed at this topic ARN, publishing forged or noise anomaly notifications that page on-call or mask a real Bedrock spend anomaly
Alert-channel spoofing/DoS: attacker floods the spend-cap topic via costalerts principal from any account
